body.x: Sunny Wave Tech (CEO Hak-sun Kim) participated in the 'Startup Zone' at the Eureka Park K-STARTUP integrated hall of 'CES 2023' in Las Vegas, USA from January 5 (Thursday) to 8 (Sunday, local time) for a total of 4 days.
Sunny Wave Tech is developing B2B and B2C target IT products based on the development of innovative technologies (securing patents) for dogs and cats.

At CES 2023, the company introduced 'DOGSPLAY', an IoT pet care device exclusively for dogs and cats. This product and app service is designed for pet owners who have to leave their pets alone at home for long periods of time, and features a CCTV, two-way communication, and a dedicated content autoplayer.

The exclusive display for dogs and cats, DOGSPLAY, has an image processing algorithm that adjusts for color blindness, malignant myopia, and dynamic visual acuity in dogs. Dogs can enjoy content that suits their preferences through the product, and can also enjoy immediate video calls with their owners. When a dog approaches the product, it can automatically turn on, and the owner can receive real-time notifications about this. The owner can also make a call or use the CCTV function for one-way monitoring. This innovative technology has been patented.

A Sunny Wave Tech representative said, "We developed this product with the goal of improving the psychological instability of dogs and cats left alone at home, such as separation anxiety, and also to alleviate the feeling of guilt of owners who leave their pets alone for long periods of time. We wanted to provide something to make the pets more happy and stable while they wait for their owners. We aim to continue to improve this innovative and groundbreaking product to help both animals and humans live happier and more stable lives."

Furthermore, the representative shared, “We conducted verification through a two-month trial with a POC product of this device. The proportion of dogs that (sometimes or often) watched TV was 29%, but 64% of dogs watched content through DOGSPLAY showing significant results.

Currently, the development of DOGSPLAY through POC has been completed, and Sunny Wave Tech is verifying the performance and marketability through user testing and feedback while optimizing practical improvement points such as design and UI that meet the needs of consumers. From the first half of 2023, starting with a crowdfunding campaign, we are preparing to expand to online or offline markets in the second half (August). In addition, Sunny Wave Tech is developing an algorithm that automatically recommends and plays content that pets like, which will be provided on a platform called 'DOGFLIX' through DOGSPLAY.

A representative said, 'We are actively seeking investment to launch a full-fledged market capitalization campaign for DOGSPLAY, and are applying for a national venture fund program. Through this upcoming CES, we are looking for local partners and global investors for global sales, and we are seeking synergistic collaboration opportunities with pet-tech companies, and through this, we are seeking new markets.'

‘CES’ is the world’s biggest IT trade show and is a place where one can see the direction and trends of the appliance industry of the entire world. Hosted by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), it is held annually in Las Vegas, USA in January. Having reported on CES for 17 consecutive years, AVING News started reporting news of CES to the entire world since 2006, and conducted ‘BEST OF CES’, which chose the most innovative product and technology, and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA, which chose the best innovative company in Korea. In addition, it vividly relayed on-site issues in CES through ‘AVING LIVE’.

The K-STARTUP Joint Pavilion featured joint participation of institutions like the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development, Seoul Business Agency, and Seoul Digital Foundation, as well as 51 Korean innovative companies, to enter the US market and discover global partners. In addition, university student supporters of CES 2023 chosen by each university (Kyunghee, Kookmin, Sogang, Chung-Ang) matched to participating companies based on their respective majors and fields of business.
